A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LLM-RankFusion. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original TREC-DL2019 ranking experiments, inconsistency measurements, component ablations, aggregation results and inference-throughput measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds TREC-DL2020 results, comparisons with additional ranking approaches and a prompt-sensitivity study.

M1.justification: v2 extends aggregation to setwise rankers and mixtures of pairwise and setwise ranking schemes, demonstrated in Table 6. Algorithm 1 correspondingly generalizes PAIRWISERANKING to RANKING. The ICL demonstration, calibration procedure and Borda aggregation rule remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates TREC-DL2019 only. v2 adds TREC-DL2020 in Tables 5–6, extending benchmark coverage while retaining the same passage-reranking task and information-retrieval domain.

E2.justification: v1's evaluated comparisons concern pairwise rankers, sorting algorithms and LLM variants. v2 Table 5 adds Setwise and Listwise (RankGPT) alongside PRP-Sort, while Table 6 includes setwise sorting configurations. This substantially broadens comparison beyond pairwise-ranking variants.

E3.justification: The existing top-100 BM25 retrieval setup and NDCG/Kendall-tau metrics remain. Added protocols include the two-model, BM25-initialized scheme comparisons in Table 6 and testing ten prompt templates with Llama-3-8B, two sorting algorithms and four component configurations in Appendix A.7. These additions do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix A.7 adds a focused sensitivity study varying prompt wording, formatting and instruction style. Table 15 tests whether ICL and calibration improve performance and stability across those variations. Existing component ablations, hard-list tests, initial-order analyses and the passage-ranking case study are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations for the 100-ordering experiments and omit Kendall-tau standard deviations. The new prompt-sensitivity table uses the existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting practice across varied conditions; no new seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results in Tables 5, 6 and 15; matched earlier results retain their values. New DL2020 scores include 65.10 for pairwise ICL plus calibration versus RankGPT's 65.49. The new prompt study reports Bubblesort scores of 62.68 ± 3.07 for baseline and 70.84 ± 1.61 with both components. These are additional comparisons, not revisions of the original result cells.

T1.justification: The core inconsistency definitions, calibration equations and Borda formulation remain unchanged, with no new theorem, proof or substantive derivation. Removing the explanatory average-Kendall-tau formula and sorting illustration does not establish a changed mathematical property or metric.

C1.justification: v1 already notes that inconsistency definitions can extend beyond pairwise ranking. v2 elevates this into an abstract/introduction claim of relevance to any ranking scheme based on relative preferences and explicitly includes setwise aggregation in its contributions. The central inconsistency-mitigation claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of scheme aggregation and prompt robustness. Its new claim that model aggregation consistently outperforms individual models conflicts with Table 6's setwise rows. Section 5.4 also changes the runtime discussion from summed individual times to slowest-model latency conditional on parallel execution.

D1.justification: Appendix A.7 documents GPT-4 generation of ten varied prompt templates. Conversely, Section 5.1 drops v1's explicit 43-query count and detailed explanation of averaging Kendall-tau distances across queries and initial orderings. Model identifiers, decoding temperature, hardware, example prompt and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 50 works are cited. The related-work taxonomy, rationale for Borda count and novelty positioning around transitive inconsistency remain substantively unchanged. Adding the Vicuna reference's URL is a bibliographic edit.

P1.justification: The six-section main narrative remains, with targeted revisions to the abstract, introduction, inconsistency explanation and experimental discussion. Limitations and future work move into the reorganized appendix. Author order and corresponding-author markers also change, without extensive rewriting of the retained text.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially reorganized: v2 adds Tables 5, 6 and 15, promotes the detailed multi-model table from the appendix while dropping its redundant summary, and moves the Kendall-tau table into the appendix. v1's explanatory Figure 2 is removed; the pipeline figure and passage/prompt displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional benchmark, setwise/RankGPT comparisons and prompt-sensitivity study make the empirical evidence more informative than v1's narrower evaluation. The net gain is limited by inaccurate superiority summaries: Table 5 favors RankGPT on DL2020, and Table 6 contains setwise aggregation results below the strongest individual model. Removing the detailed Kendall-tau averaging explanation also weakens reproducibility.
